plugins.readme_text:
# opencode2dsh **Free OpenCode Zen models, natively inside DSH (DeepSeek Harness).** No API key. No registration. No extra process. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/blob/master/LICENSE) [![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-brightgreen)](https://nodejs.org) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-blue)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh) English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
--- opencode2dsh registers a native DSH `LlmAdapter` that streams directly from [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/zen)'s **anonymous free lane** — the same models OpenCode's own CLI uses without an account, served to your DSH model picker as a regular provider called `opencode2dsh`. Requests leave your machine looking exactly like traffic from the OpenCode CLI (same user agent, same correlation headers), and the model catalog stays fresh through a three-tier fallback chain. There is nothing to log into and nothing to host. ## Highlights - **Zero credential, zero setup** — the anonymous lane needs no key; install, restart, chat - **Native adapter, no sidecar** — one npm package, no child process, no binary, no local port (the legacy Go sidecar is not part of the published package; see `legacy/`) - **CLI-identical disguise** — requests carry the OpenCode CLI user agent and its session/request/project header set, derived per conversation - **Selectable thinking levels** — reasoning-capable free models expose an effort picker in DSH's model selector (declared ladders where the model metadata provides them, Off/Minimal/Low/Medium/High otherwise); Responses-only `muse-spark-*` models expose only upstream-supported effort levels, and no selection keeps the provider default - **Image input where it is declared** — image attachments are accepted for every model whose [models.dev](https://models.dev) entry lists `image` in `modalities.input`, and refused for the ones that declare `text` only; models.dev being silent falls back to the live-verified vision family - **Live catalog with a fallback chain** — live upstream list ∩ free-by-metadata, falling back to offline cache and a verified static list - **Self-healing** — fast startup retries, periodic refresh, and a written health snapshot for diagnostics - **Proper error surfaces** — upstream failures (rate limit, auth, timeout, transport) arrive in DSH as classified finish reasons, and retries stay owned by DSH ## Install **From the plugin market** (recommended, once this repo is listed there): in DSH open **Settings → Plugin Market**, search `opencode2dsh`, one-click install. **From npm**: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin ``` **From source** (build the tarball yourself): ```sh git clone https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh.git cd opencode2dsh/packages/plugin pnpm install && pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile web add ./opencode2dsh-dsh-plugin-.tgz ``` **Verify**: restart `dsh web`, open the model picker, and pick a model from the **opencode2dsh** group. Requires DSH (DeepSeek Harness) 0.1.7 or newer with a web profile (the IP 池 settings page rides the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract); Node.js ≥ 20 (already present if DSH runs); outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` and `models.dev`. ## Configuration Defaults work out of the box. Override via the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: opencode2dsh name: '@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin' config: mode: adapter # adapter (default) | sidecar providerId: opencode2dsh refreshSeconds: 300 # catalog refresh cadence ``` | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `mode` | `adapter` | `adapter`: native LlmAdapter streaming straight from Zen. `sidecar`: legacy local-agent mode, not bundled — build the agent from `legacy/agent` and pass `agentPath`. | | `providerId` | `opencode2dsh` | Provider name shown in DSH. | | `refreshSeconds` | `300` | Live catalog refresh interval. Pricing metadata refreshes every 24 h. | | `agentPath` | auto-resolved | Sidecar only: path to the agent binary. | | `agentArgs` | — | Sidecar only: extra CLI args for the agent. | | `restartDelayMs` / `restartMaxDelayMs` / `maxConsecutiveCrashes` | `1000` / `60000` / `5` | Sidecar only: restart backoff and circuit breaker. | | `firstEventMs` / `bodyIdleMs` / `responsesBodyIdleMs` | `30000` / `120000` / `300000` | Adapter only, plugin 0.3.7+: stream-liveness watchdogs, in ms (integers from `1` to `600000`). Time to the first stream event, mid-response body silence, and the body-idle floor for Responses models (`muse-spark-*`). Increase `firstEventMs` for slow cold starts. Unset keeps the defaults; restart DSH after editing. | ## How it works ``` DSH session │ harness chunks (block-start / text-delta / usage / finish …) ▼ ZenAdapter (registered LlmAdapter) │ pi-ai openai-completions stream (chat models) │ pi-ai openai-responses stream (`muse-spark-*`, Responses-only on Zen) ▼ https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 ← Authorization: Bearer public with CLI-identical headers: user-agent: opencode/… x-opencode-client, x-opencode-session, x-session-affinity, X-Session-Id, x-opencode-request, x-opencode-project ``` - **Session correlation** — session/project ids are SHA-256 derived from the conversation's first user turn (stable per conversation, non-reversible), and each request gets a fresh random id, mirroring the CLI. - **Catalog fallback chain** — S1: live `GET /v1/models`; S2: models.dev pricing metadata decides "free"; S3: a compile-time verified static list. A disk cache (~7-day TTL) covers upstream outages. - **Resilience** — the adapter registers immediately at startup; if the first catalog fetch races your network (VPN/TUN reconnects, DNS), the plugin retries on a short cadence (~1 min) before settling into the periodic refresh. - **Sidecar mode** (`mode: sidecar`, legacy) — spawns a local Go agent (a single-tenant port of [opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api)) on `127.0.0.1:`, token-authenticated, and registers a standard `llm-pi-ai` route. **Not part of the published package**; build it from `legacy/agent` (`go build ./cmd/agent`) and point `agentPath` at the binary. ## Health & troubleshooting The plugin writes a health snapshot after every refresh round: ``` ~/.opencode2dsh/adapter-status.json ``` ```json { "status": "ready", "total": 64, "exposed": 9, "lastError": "", "writtenAt": "2026-08-29T07:01:54.915Z" } ``` | Symptom | Likely cause & fix | | --- | --- | | `403 FreeTierError` / "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode" | The upstream restricts free-tier clients. The plugin preserves the explanation instead of reporting an invalid API key. Use the supported OpenCode client or an official API service. | | Boot screen shows `Failed to load plugins … list slot "plugins.item" requires options.id`, or the IP 池 entry has no configuration page | Your DSH predates the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract. Upgrade DSH to 0.1.7 (latest recommended). On 0.1.6 and older the page never mounts (it is gated on `configForms.whileServed`) — model routing is unaffected. | | DSH 0.1.7/0.2 cannot start after plugin installation (`pending … settingsScope`) | Upgrade the plugin to 0.3.5. On DSH 0.2, configure IP pooling through the installed opencode2dsh row on the Plugins page. | | Only 3 models | Startup fetch raced your network; retries land within ~1 min. Check `adapter-status.json` for `lastError`. | | `lastError: "fetch failed"` persisting | Outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` blocked; check proxy/VPN rules. | | Rate-limit errors in chat (`429 … Endpoint is unavailable`) | The anonymous lane is quota-per-IP and free models are contended. Since the fix for [#51](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/issues/51) the plugin's provider retry policy rides out 429 bursts silently (8 retries, ~1s→20s backoff, ≈90s worst case per step) instead of sur

plugins.description: DSH Web 全局皮肤插件：图片/视频背景铺满界面，面板半透明可调 | Global image/video background skin for DSH Web
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-skin-live

把一张图片或一段视频铺满整个 DSH Web 界面 —— **只改背景，不动布局**。 插件在页面最底层挂一个固定画布，把应用本身的底色透明化，于是主区域和侧栏共用同一张背景；卡片、输入框、弹层仍留在原位置、原尺寸，只是变成了半透明玻璃。所有参数存在浏览器本地，素材不上传、不联网。 - 图片：`PNG` `JPG` `JPEG` `WebP` `GIF` `AVIF` `BMP` `SVG` - 视频：`MP4` `WebM` `OGV` `MOV` `M4V` `MKV`（静音、循环、自动播放） - 也可以直接填一个图片 / 视频 URL，素材不用下载到本地 - 四项独立调节：面板不透明度、素材不透明度、模糊、暗化 - 停用或卸载插件后，背景层被移除、主题变量还原，界面回到默认外观 ## 目录 - [安装](#安装) - [使用](#使用) - [参数说明](#参数说明) - [兼容范围](#兼容范围) - [卸载与回滚](#卸载与回滚) - [数据与隐私](#数据与隐私) - [与其它皮肤插件共存](#与其它皮肤插件共存) - [本地开发](#本地开发) - [许可](#许可) ## 安装 DSH 自带插件管理器，三种来源都支持。**任选一种即可，不需要手改配置文件。** ### 方式一：Web 插件页（推荐，不用命令行） 1. 打开 DSH Web 界面（默认 ）。 2. 左侧栏进入 **插件**（Plugins）页。 3. 在安装输入框里粘贴下面这一行，确认安装： ``` github:zhaochaorui-study/dsh-skin-live ``` 4. 安装完成后插件会默认启用；如果列表里显示未启用，手动打开它的开关。 5. 刷新页面（`Cmd/Ctrl + R`），设置里就会出现「皮肤」。 ### 方式二：命令行 ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add github:zhaochaorui-study/dsh-skin-live ``` 发布到 npm 之后，也可以直接用包名： ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-skin-live ``` > `--profile web` 是目标 profile 名。桌面版换用 `--profile desktop`（尚未验证）。 ### 方式三：离线安装包 `.tgz` 不想联网或想固定版本时，从 [Releases](https://github.com/zhaochaorui-study/dsh-skin-live/releases) 下载 `dsh-skin-live-1.0.0.tgz`，然后： ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add /绝对路径/dsh-skin-live-1.0.0.tgz ``` 也可以在插件页选择这个本地文件安装。 ### 验证安装 ```bash dsh plugin --profile web list | grep dsh-skin-live dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A2 'dsh-skin-live' ``` 预期能看到 `dsh-skin-live` 这一条依赖，以及一个 `id: dsh-skin-live` 的加载项。 ## 使用 界面里的路径是 **设置 → 皮肤**。 1. **选择背景** —— 点「选择文件」上传，或把图片 / 视频直接拖进虚线框；也可以在输入框里粘贴素材 URL。 2. **调节参数** —— 按下面的表格拖动滑块，画面实时变化。 3. **自动保存** —— 参数写入 `localStorage`，素材写入 `IndexedDB`，刷新或重启 DSH 后自动恢复。 首版的完整流程就是这三步：**安装插件 → 选择背景 → 调整模糊和暗化**。 ## 参数说明 | 控件 | 范围 | 作用 | | --- | --- | --- | | 启用皮肤 | 开 / 关 | 临时关掉背景层并还原主题，素材和参数都保留，随时开回来 | | 背景来源 | 文件 / URL | 本地文件存进 `IndexedDB`；URL 每次加载时直接引用 | | 铺满方式 | 铺满 / 完整 / 拉伸 | 对应 `object-fit: cover / contain / fill` | | 面板不透明度 | 0–100% | 只作用于卡片、输入框、弹层等面板表面；0% 为全透明，100% 为当前主题原色 | | 素材不透明度 | 10–100% | 背景图片 / 视频本身的透明度 | | 模糊 | 0–40px | 只模糊背景层，文字保持清晰（模糊时自动放大 6% 避免边缘露白） | | 暗化 | 0–80% | 在背景上叠一层黑色蒙版，深色主题下更好读 | 侧栏属于全局背景画布，所以它跟随背景显示；「面板不透明度」不会把它单独盖掉。 ## 兼容范围 | 环境 | 状态 | | --- | --- | | DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` + Web / PWA | ✅ 已实测 | | DSH Desktop（`--profile desktop`） | ⚠️ 未验证，按需自行确认 | | 更早的 DSH 版本 | 未验证；插件依赖 `slots` / `theme` / `locale` 三个客户端服务 | 实现上刻意**不声明 `peerDependencies`**，避免 DSH 运行时升级后出现版本互斥拒绝安装；服务缺失或接口变化时，插件会退化为无背景，不会影响主界面正常使用。 主题相关的实现依赖 DSH 的主题服务（`theme.overrideTokens`）、调色板变量（`--dsw-alias-*`、`--dsw-specific-*`）和插槽 / 语言服务，DSH 升级后如果变量被重命名，面板不透明度会回落到主题默认值（不会出现错误颜色）。 ## 卸载与回滚 **停用（保留数据）**：插件页关掉开关，或在设置里关掉「启用皮肤」——背景立刻还原，参数和素材都还在。 **彻底卸载**： ```bash dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-skin-live ``` 然后在插件页确认它已从列表消失，刷新页面。卸载后 `localStorage` / `IndexedDB` 里的参数与素材可以手动清理： ```js // 浏览器开发者工具 Console localStorage.removeItem('dsh-skin-live:settings:v1'); indexedDB.deleteDatabase('dsh-skin-live:media'); ``` ## 数据与隐私 - 参数：`localStorage` 键 `dsh-skin-live:settings:v1` - 素材：`IndexedDB` 库 `dsh-skin-live:media`，对象仓库 `blobs`，键 `current` - 插件不发起任何网络请求，也不上报数据。填 URL 时，素材由浏览器按该地址直接加载。 从早期本地版 `@local/dsh-skin-live` 升级过来时，旧键 `@local/dsh-skin-live:settings:v1` 和旧库 `@local/dsh-skin-live:media` 里的内容会被自动沿用并复制一份到新名字下；旧数据不会被删除，方便回退到旧版本。 ## 与其它皮肤插件共存 如果同时装了另一套皮肤系统（例如 `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-skin-center`），两边都会改写背景和主题变量，会互相覆盖。建议只保留一套。 ## 本地开发 仓库结构： ``` . ├── package.json # dsh 清单：bundle patch、client 入口、注入的客户端服务 ├── index.js # Host 半边：只提供 Loader 条目，不做事 ├── client.js # Client 半边：背景层、主题 token、设置页（全部逻辑） ├── client.test.js # 回归测试（node:test + 最小 DOM/IndexedDB 夹具） ├── cordis.patch.yml # 插件挂载声明 ├── locale/ # 设置页文案 └── icon.svg # 插件图标 ``` 跑检查： ```bash npm run check # 两个入口的语法检查 npm test # 9 项回归测试 npm pack # 产出可安装的 .tgz ``` 手工 link 到本机 profile 调试、以及从旧版本迁移本机配置的完整步骤，见 [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)。 ### 设计取舍 - 背景层是 `position: fixed; z-index: -1` 且 `pointer-events: none` 的独立节点，挂在 `document.body` 上 —— 这是既能垫在整个应用之下、又不影响页面原有布局的唯一位置。 - 面板半透明走主题变量覆盖（`theme.overrideTokens`），逐个 token 读取当前主题的真实色值再混入透明度；主题没定义的 token 直接跳过，而不是猜一个颜色。 - 所有副作用都挂在 `ctx.effect` 上，插件卸载时移除 DOM、撤销 token 覆盖、释放对象 URL。 - 插件本体很轻（几十 KB），不带任何素材；皮肤素材由用户自己提供，因此安装包可以保持小体积。 ## 许可 [MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: Noema long-term memory plugin for DSH: durable, inspectable agent memory with recall tools and a settings page.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Noema

Long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness — durable, inspectable agent memory backed by Noema.
Recall Before Work • Import From 9 Agent Tools • Settings-Page Memory Management • Crash Keep-Alive • Hot Reload

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-noema · Tested with DSH 0.2.0-rc.2

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The Noema Memory settings page — import sources, memory management, and live server status

## Why DSH Noema DSH Noema connects [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) with [Noema](https://github.com/ZSeven-W/noema) — a local-first, non-vector memory system for coding agents — so an Agent keeps durable knowledge across sessions instead of starting every conversation from zero.
### 🧠 Durable Recall Memories persist as inspectable Markdown files under `NOEMA_ROOT` (default `~/.agent-memory/`). `noema_recall` loads relevant context at the start of a session; `noema_search`, `noema_browse`, `noema_catalog`, and `noema_recall_graph` cover lookup, exploration, and auditing. ### 📥 Import From Other Tools `noema_import` reads the memory files of ten other AI coding tools — Codex, Claude Code, opencode, Cursor, Grok, WorkBuddy, Antigravity, Trae, Qoder, Hermes — splits them into sections, and saves each as a durable memory. A content-keyed ledger deduplicates across runs and across tools that share files.
### 🛠️ Settings-Page Management The Noema Memory settings page configures the server command, memory root, budgets, idle/call timeouts, and the guidance section — and a Manage memories card searches, browses, adds, reviews, and deletes stored memories directly. ### 🩺 Keep-Alive The memory server stays up: idle timeout defaults to never, and a keep-alive loop restarts the `noema-mcp` child in the background when it crashes or exits, with a configurable check interval and restart backoff.
### 🔍 Smart Entity Extraction Noema's extraction engine combines jieba word segmentation with high-precision signals — English proper nouns, CJK names and technical terms, quoted topics, and repetition — with stopword and path filters, so the PageIndex topic catalog stays clean. ### ⚡ Hot Reload After the first boot, the plugin never needs a restart again: `pnpm run build` hot-reloads the host plugin through Cordis HMR, and `ppnpm run build:client` hot-swaps the browser bundle over the client-hmr SSE channel.
## Install into DSH ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-noema@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-noema dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately and Cordis HMR can watch the compiled output. The plugin bundles the `noema-mcp` binary through per-platform optional npm packages. To build it yourself instead, run `cargo build --release -p noema-mcp` inside the bundled `noema` submodule, or point the Server command setting at any `noema-mcp` build. ## Memory Tools The model-facing tools mirror the Noema MCP surface: | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `noema_recall` | Recall relevant memories for a query, with a token budget. | | `noema_search` | Full-text search over stored memories. | | `noema_browse` | Browse the PageIndex catalog for a topic or entity. | | `noema_catalog` | Render the full memory catalog as markdown. | | `noema_recall_graph` | Multi-hop recall through links and shared entities. | | `noema_neighbors` | One graph hop from a memory. | | `noema_explain` | Explain why a memory was or was not recalled. | | `noema_remember` | Save a durable fact, decision, constraint, or preference. | | `noema_review_list` | List pending review candidates. | | `noema_review_decide` | Accept, reject, edit, or merge a candidate. | | `noema_forget` | Tombstone or hard-delete a memory. | | `noema_policy_get` / `noema_policy_set` | Read or update the write policy. | | `noema_status` | Server and tenant status: counts, index health, storage root. | | `noema_import` | Import memories from other AI coding tools. | Each tool returns a uniform envelope `{ ok, tool, text }` where `text` carries the full server output. ## Import memories from other tools | Source id | Global files | Workspace files | | --- | --- | --- | | `codex` | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` + the Codex memory pipeline: `~/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md`, `memory_summary.md`, `rollout_summaries/*.md`, `extensions/ad_hoc/notes/*.md` (`raw_memories.md` skipped — it is the uncurated feed) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` | | `claude-code` | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.local.md`, `~/.claude/MEMORY.md` | `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `MEMORY.md` | | `opencode` | `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` | | `cursor` | `~/.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `~/.cursorrules` | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.cursorrules` | | `grok` | `~/.grok/AGENTS.md` + the Grok cross-session memory: `~/.grok/memory/MEMORY.md`, per-project `MEMORY.md`, and `sessions/*.md` summaries | `AGENTS.md` | | `workbuddy` | `~/.codebuddy/CODEBUDDY.md` (WorkBuddy memory file), `~/.workbuddy/AGENTS.md`, `~/.workbuddy/memory.md`, `~/.config/workbuddy/AGENTS.md`, `~/Library/Application Support/WorkBuddy/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md`, `CODEBUDDY.md` | | `antigravity` | `~/.antigravity/AGENTS.md`, `~/.config/antigravity/AGENTS.md`, `~/Library/Application Support/Antigravity/AGENTS.md` (best-effort; no documented global memory store yet) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` | | `trae` | `~/.trae/AGENTS.md`, `~/.trae/memory/`, `~/.trae/rules/` (plus the `~/.trae-cn` variants) | `AGENTS.md`, `.trae/rules/` | | `qoder` | `~/.qoder-cn/AGENTS.md`, `~/.qoder-cn/rules/`, the auto-memory roots `~/.qoder-cn/memory/` and `~/.qoder-cn/projects/*/memory/` (plus `~/.qoder` variants) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md`, `.qoder/rules/` | | `hermes` | `~/.hermes/memories/` (`MEMORY.md` + `USER.md`) and the global `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` | `.hermes.md`, `HERMES.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | - The `source` argument selects one tool, or omit it to run every source enabled in settings. - The `path` argument selects the workspace root for project-scoped files (defaults to the session workspace; workspace files only load when the Import workspace files setting is on). - Imports are deduplicated through a ledger at `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-noema-imports.json`, keyed by file path +

plugins.description: Favorites, copy id+path, per-session delete, idle batch archive and a favourites filter for DSH conversations — additive slot extensions over the shipped archive feature, editing no official file. 为 DSH 对话增加收藏、复制 ID+路径、单条删除、超时批量归档与收藏筛选。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-archive-favorites-forge

**Favourites, copy id+path, per-session delete, idle batch archive and a
favourites filter for DeepSeek Harness conversations** — additive slot
extensions over the shipped archive feature. It edits **no official file**.

**给 DSH 的对话加上收藏、复制 ID+路径、单条删除、超时批量归档和收藏筛选 —— 全部挂在官方插槽上，不改官方一行代码。**

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-dsh--archive--favorites--forge-cb3837?logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-archive-favorites-forge)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%E2%89%A5%200.2.0--rc.2-4f46e5)](https://github.com/loyalchiiina/dsh-archive-favorites-forge)

English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

---

## Screenshots

**1. The conversation menu** — favourite, copy id + path, and a guarded permanent delete, added as three rows to the shipped 「…」 menu:

![Session menu](assets/01-session-menu.png)

**2. The favourites filter** — two extra rows in the official 筛选会话 group, narrowing the sidebar to favourites that are archived and to favourites that are not:

![Favourites filter](assets/02-favourites-filter.png)

**3. The settings panel** — idle batch archive, the favourites list with archive state, and batch delete of archived conversations that are not favourites:

![Settings panel](assets/03-settings-panel.png)

---

## Why this exists

DSH already ships an archive feature: the Workspace registry keeps a global
`archivedSessionIds` set and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` renders the
sidebar rows plus a view-options filter. That shipped feature has **no
favourites, no per-conversation delete, no copy-id/path affordance, and no
time-based batch archive** — and it deliberately refuses to open an archived
conversation.

This plugin adds those things by attaching to documented official slot points,
so it composes with the shipped UI instead of patching it.

## Features · At a glance

| | 中文 | English |
|---|---|---|
| ① | **收藏对话**：归档或未归档的对话都能收藏；「…」菜单项 + 行内 ☆，星标即时生效 | **Favourite any conversation** — archived or not; a menu row plus an inline ☆ star, applied optimistically |
| ② | **复制 ID + 路径**：「…」菜单一键复制会话 ID 与转录文件绝对路径（两行） | **Copy id + path** — one menu row copying the session id and the transcript's absolute path |
| ③ | **单条永久删除**：任意非收藏对话可删，二次确认；删完侧栏**立即移除该行** | **Per-conversation permanent delete** — any non-favourite, behind a confirmation, and the sidebar row disappears at once |
| ④ | **超时批量归档**：把闲置超过 N 小时的未归档对话一次性归档，可撤回 | **Idle batch archive** — archives conversations quiet for more than N hours, undoable |
| ⑤ | **导出清单**：制表符分隔的 txt，含**对话名称 / 对话ID / 所属工作区 / 闲置时长 / 最后活动时间**；可复制路径或直接打开所在文件夹 | **Export list** — a tab-separated txt with name, id, workspace, idle time and last-activity time; copy its path or reveal it in the file manager |
| ⑥ | **收藏筛选**：视图选项菜单新增「仅显示收藏（已归档）」与「仅显示收藏（未归档）」 | **Favourites filter** — view-options rows for favourites that are archived, and favourites that are not |
| ⑦ | **批量删除**：一键永久删除「已归档且未收藏」的对话 | **Batch delete** — permanently removes the archived-and-unfavourited conversations |
| ⑧ | **删除护栏**：收藏项拒删、越出会话根目录拒删、符号链接拒删、逐条报告、批量上限 | **Delete guardrails** — favourites refused, paths outside the sessions root refused, symlinks refused, per-id reporting, batch cap |

### Where each feature lives

| Feature | UI location |
|---|---|
| Favourite / copy / delete one conversation | Sidebar row 「…」 menu (and a hover ☆ on the row) |
| Idle batch archive, export list, favourites list, batch delete | **Settings → 归档收藏** |
| Favourites filter | **视图选项 → 筛选会话** |

## Install

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-archive-favorites-forge
```

Then **fully quit and reopen DSH**. The host half (`lib/index.js`) has no
watcher in this harness generation, and the client bundle is snapshotted at
startup — so a page refresh alone does **not** pick up a new version.

## How it works

```
lib/index.js    host half   — favourites store, transcript-path resolver,
                              JSON routes, guarded delete, archive/dearchive
lib/client.js   client half — official slot registrations + one DOM rule
```

**Slots used** (all documented in the harness client contract):

| Slot | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` | 3 rows: favourite, copy id+path, delete |
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.row.action` | 1 hover ☆ star |
| `settings.section` | the 归档收藏 page |

Every contribution is registered through `ctx.slots.inject` — the "register once
the owning entry is mounted" contract — so the plugin never assumes the sidebar
is up, and never holds a reference to a node the host owns.

The favourites filter is the one exception: the view-options menu is a plain
array with **no slot and no trigger id**, so that single control is added by
finding the official filter row in the DOM and cloning it. It keys on
`role`/`aria`/`data-row-key` attributes, never on the CSS-module hashes (which
are re-hashed on every build).

### Why the favourites set lives in a file, not `localStorage`

Renderer `localStorage` is origin-scoped: the desktop shell, a phone view and a
remote browser are different origins and would each keep their own stars. The
host half persists them to

```
~/.dsh/data/dsh-archive-favorites-forge/favorites.json
```

which survives a profile switch, a reinstall, and both ends.

### Why the delete is host-side and guarded

There is **no official session-delete RPC** in this harness generation — the
shipped UI never deletes a session. "Delete this conversation" therefore means
removing the session's own artifact directory under `~/.dsh/sessions/`. That is
irreversible, so the host applies these guards before it removes anything:

1. a **favourited** id is refused outright (checked host-side, not just in the UI);
2. a resolved path **outside the sessions root** is refused;
3. a **symlink** is refused;
4. the sessions root itself is refused;
5. the batch is capped by `maxDeletePerCall`.

Each id is reported separately, so one failure never aborts the batch. After a
successful delete the host emits `api-session/removed` — the harness's own
row-removal event — so the sidebar drops the row immediately instead of showing
it until the next reload.

## Configuration

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch for the host routes |
| `maxDeletePerCall` | `500` | Hard cap on one delete request |

```yaml
- id: dsh-archive-favorites-forge
  config:
    maxDeletePerCall: 200
```

## Notes and limits

- **The id form**: session ids are spelled `session-<uuid>`, but artifact
  directories on an upgraded machine use **both** `<uuid>` and `session-<uuid>`.
  Every comparison goes through a normaliser and the resolver tries both
  spellings, so this works for old and new conversations alike.
- **Archived conversations cannot be opened** — that is shipped DSH behaviour,
  not this plugin's. Unarchive first if you want to read one.
- **Deleting is permanent.** It removes the conversation and its transcript. It
  does not touch your project working directory.
- **Blank sessions are never candidates.** A "blank" session is the provisional
  New Session slot; it has no content to archive and the shipped sidebar hides
  every blank session except the currently selected one, so a candidate list
  containing one would be impossible to verify. They are excluded from both the
  idle pool and the batch-delete set, and the export names the rest the way the
  sidebar does (`新会话` / `未命名`).
- **Candidate lists are intersected with what the sidebar actually lists.** A
  session that is archived but not rendered (no `cwd`) is never counted or
  acted on.
- The plugin reads the Workspace registry to map a session to its owning
  folder. It mutates that registry only through the registry's **own**
  `archiveSession` / `unarchiveSession` methods, and never writes another
  plugin's internals.

## Development

```
lib/index.js             host half
lib/client.js            client half (a __ModuleLoader__ bundle)
test/probe-client.mjs    DOM-stub + host probe suite
```

Run the suite:

```sh
node test/probe-client.mjs
```

The probe is not a formality — it has repeatedly caught bugs

plugins.description: Read-only CSV/XLSX change review for DeepSeek Harness: align business keys, inspect values and formulas, and export review comments.
plugins.readme_text:
# SheetDiff

Review spreadsheet changes before trusting them.

SheetDiff compares two CSV or XLSX files by a business key, not by row position. It produces a local HTML report where you can inspect values, types, formulas and stored formula results, then leave comments for a follow-up with your agent.

It is an independent DeepSeek Harness plugin. It also has a small CLI. It does not edit workbooks, calculate formulas, upload data, or require an API key.

![Local review report showing a formula change and an exported comment](docs/review-demo.jpg)

## Try it locally

Requires Node.js 22.19 or newer. Clone the repository and try the synthetic demo:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/po-et/dsh-sheet-diff.git
cd dsh-sheet-diff
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run demo
```

The demo writes two **synthetic** workbooks and a `report.html` to a new directory under `artifacts/`. Open the printed report path in a browser. The expected result is three added rows and four changed cells: two amounts, one formula with a changed stored result, and one number changed to text. Reordering rows and columns adds no changes.

For your own files:

```sh
node src/cli.js before.xlsx after.xlsx --key OrderID --out review-001
node src/cli.js examples/before.csv examples/after.csv --key OrderID --out review-csv
```

`--out` must name a new directory. Use repeated `--key` flags for a composite key. `--sheet Orders` selects one sheet; `--header-row 3` changes the header row. Otherwise, all sheets use row 1 as their header and must have the chosen key columns. CSV has one logical sheet named `CSV`.

Compare CSV with CSV, or XLSX with XLSX. Mixed-format comparisons are rejected in this release.

## Use with DeepSeek Harness

Install the versioned release bundle into a profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile YOUR_PROFILE add https://github.com/po-et/dsh-sheet-diff/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-sheet-diff-0.1.0.tgz
```

Restart that profile after installation. The package ships JavaScript and a `dsh.bundle` patch; there is no plugin build step or install script. You can also build the bundle from source with `npm pack` and install its local absolute path. Releases are distributed through [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/po-et/dsh-sheet-diff/releases); this project is not published to npm.

Tested against Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-alpha.2`, with explicit preview-version peer ranges. Both were installed into fresh profiles and exercised through the official profile boot entrypoint without a model call. HMR was disabled only in the test profiles; the source-built alpha host also logged unrelated optional Typert import warnings.

Ask Harness:

> Compare `before.xlsx` and `after.xlsx` using `OrderID` as the key. Save a SheetDiff report in `reviews/run-001`. Do not change either workbook.

The plugin registers two tools:

| Tool | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sheet_diff_compare` | `before`, `after`, `keyColumns`, `outputDir`; optional `sheet`, `headerRow` | New HTML/JSON paths, hashes, summary and warnings |
| `sheet_diff_review` | `reportJson`, `reviewJson` | Validated comments with the corresponding changes |

Paths must stay inside the current session workspace, including resolved symlink targets. Report creation needs a writable sandbox. Existing reports are never overwritten. If the second output write fails, the tool reports the retained first file rather than deleting it.

The interactive report opens in a normal browser. A Harness preview that disables JavaScript cannot run its comment controls. There is no custom in-app spreadsheet editor in this release.

## Review, then hand comments back

1. Open the HTML report, filter changes, and write comments beside the changes you want checked.
2. Export the review JSON. Draft comments stay only in page memory until exported.
3. Put the export inside the workspace and pass it, with the original report JSON, to `sheet_diff_review`.

The CLI equivalent is:

```sh
node src/cli.js review review-001/report.json review-comments.json
```

Comments must match the report ID, both input hashes and known change IDs. Old or unrelated reviews are rejected. A hash match is not a digital signature and does not prove that a report has not been deliberately rewritten. Comments and cell contents are untrusted data; this plugin never executes their instructions or applies their suggested edits.

## Comparison rules

- Column names and keys match exactly. Composite keys include cell types; numeric `42` is different from text `"42"`. Duplicate keys, missing keys and duplicate headers fail rather than being guessed.
- CSV is comma-delimited UTF-8, with quoted fields, embedded newlines and a BOM supported. Values remain text; CSV formulas are not inferred.
- XLSX preserves the distinction between numbers, text, booleans, dates, errors and formulas. Formula text and saved cached results are separate aspects of a change. A cache is **not** a fresh calculation.
- Formula caches containing an explicit empty string are rejected in v0.1: the underlying reader cannot reliably distinguish them from a missing cache. Zero and false caches are preserved.
- Formula text is compared literally. Moving a formula can change its A1 references while preserving meaning; SheetDiff does not normalize that equivalence.
- Blank rows are skipped. Added/removed rows include their populated fields. Added/removed columns produce structural changes, plus cell changes for populated values in retained rows.
- Sheet renames are reported as removal and addition. Key changes are reported as row removal and addition.

This is a table-data review tool, not a whole-workbook fidelity check. Formatting, number formats, merged layout, charts, pivots, images, comments and hyperlink targets are outside its scope. Hidden data is still read; visibility itself is not compared. Legacy XLS, macros, encrypted archives and external workbook connections are unsupported. Complex multi-table sheets may need to be exported to separate tables first.

## Limits and privacy

Inputs are capped at 20 MiB each, XLSX expanded contents at 64 MiB and 8 MiB per ZIP part, and comparisons at 10,000 change records or 24 MiB of serialized changes. The parser also caps serialized cells/rows at 100,000 and checks expanded merge, column and validation ranges before parsing. Exceeding a limit fails the comparison; a shortened report is never presented as complete.

Reports include changed cell data, source filenames and hashes. Treat HTML, report JSON and review JSON as sensitive as the workbooks. Sharing is manual. The page has no remote resources, analytics or automatic persistence. When used inside an AI host, tool results and imported comments may be sent to that host's configured model as part of its normal operation.

## Development

```sh
npm test
npm run smoke:host
npm pack --dry-run
```

`smoke:host` loads the shipped patch using a real Cordis loader and dispatches both tools through the real tool runtime, filesystem provider and sandbox policy. It also checks source bytes, overwrite rejection and plugin disposal. It uses a fresh temporary workspace; it does not change an existing Harness profile. The test is separate from a full CLI installation and does not use a live model.

## 中文简介

AI 改完表格后，先看清楚改了什么，再决定是否采用。SheetDiff 按订单号、账户号等业务主键对齐记录，避免把行列重排当成大量修改；数值、类型、公式和保存的计算结果分开显示。你可以在本地报告中逐条评论，导出后交回 Harness 继续处理。

首版只读 CSV/XLSX，不上传表格、不重算公式、不自动改文件。它不是表格编辑器，也不承诺检测格式、图表或所有 Excel 功能的变化。

MIT licensed. Bug reports are most useful with a small anonymized example and the expected comparison result. Please do not post confidential workbooks.

plugins.description: Use your Zed AI subscription (Pro / Student) from DeepSeek Harness: registers the zed-agent route with Claude + GPT models, an editable Models-page card and a model chooser.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-zed-provider

Run your **Zed AI subscription** (Zed Pro / Student — the monthly prompt credits)
inside DeepSeek Harness. The bundle registers one LLM provider route,
`zed-agent`, whose turns are minted and streamed through Zed Cloud
(`https://cloud.zed.dev`) exactly as the Zed editor does it.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-zed-provider
```

## Link your Zed account

Type `/zed-login` in the Harness composer. The command opens Zed's native-app
sign-in page, waits for the loopback callback, and stores the resulting grant in
the Harness credential store (`llm-zed/zed-agent`). Later requests reuse it, and
the short-lived gateway token is minted automatically and refreshed on demand.

Credentials are resolved in this order, so any one of them is enough:

1. `config.credentials` — a literal `"<userId> <accessToken>"` (or JSON) value.
2. `config.apiKeyEnv` (default `ZED_CREDENTIALS`) — resolved through the
   credential seam. The Models settings page shows this as the Zed card's key
   field, so a credential pasted there works without `/zed-login`.
3. The `llm-zed/zed-agent` grant record written by `/zed-login`.
4. The Zed editor's own local keyring entry, on macOS (`zed.dev`) and Linux
   (`secret-tool`), imported once into the grant record — sign in inside Zed and
   this plugin picks it up by itself.

`apiKeyEnv` is spelled that way because the Models page reads exactly that field
name; its value is a credential *reference*, and what it holds is the
`"<userId> <accessToken>"` pair Zed issues.

## Settings UI

Settings → **Models** → the **Zed** card carries this bundle's own editor
(`lib/client.js`, a client-module half registered on the page's
`settings.models.provider-card` seat for the `llm-zed` namespace):

- credential status, from the card's credential join plus a live
  `credentials/describe`;
- a credential field that stores `"<userId> <accessToken>"` under the reference
  `apiKeyEnv` names (read live from the settings document, default
  `ZED_CREDENTIALS`), with **Remove** to unset it;
- a refusal instead of a silent no-op when that reference is supplied by a
  read-only source such as an environment variable.

It also carries the **model chooser**: the Host registers
`llm.registerModelDiscovery` for this namespace, the page reads it through
`llm/discoverModels`, and the tick boxes write `visibleModels` through
`settings/mutate`. That field is volatile, so a tick changes the picker on the
next catalog read without a reload; an empty or complete selection unsets it,
meaning "offer every model this plugin can run".

`baseUrl` stays a composition-only field in `cordis.patch.yml`.

The client fiber hard-injects only `slots`, `locale` and `remote`, and picks the
credential remote up through `ctx.inject(['remote.credentials'], …)`. That is
deliberate: the web boot asserts that every client entry activated, so a root
client plugin that waits on a service the settings UI keeps private (such as
`settingsScope`) takes the whole GUI boot down with
`<package>: pending (waiting for service: …)`.

## Models

`listModels` reads `GET /models` with your credential and advertises the models
Zed reports for the backends this plugin implements — **Claude** (Anthropic
Messages) and **GPT** (OpenAI Responses). Zed's Gemini and Grok entries are
filtered out rather than offered broken; selecting one anyway fails fast with
`UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT`.

Each model carries Zed's own context window, output cap, and — when
`supports_thinking` — the effort levels `off` / `low` / `high` / `max`, mapped
onto Anthropic extended thinking budgets.

## Configuration

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `apiKeyEnv` | `ZED_CREDENTIALS` | Credential reference holding `"<userId> <accessToken>"`. |
| `credentials` | absent | Literal credential value; highest priority, composition-time. |
| `baseUrl` | `https://cloud.zed.dev` | Zed Cloud endpoint. |
| `visibleModels` | all supported | Narrow the catalog to these model ids. |

## Quota

Zed owns the accounting: no plan or no credits left answers HTTP 402, which
surfaces as a `QUOTA` failure naming https://zed.dev/account. The plugin does
not invent percentages or limits.

## Development

`pnpm install` (which runs the `prepare` hook), then `pnpm check` —
typecheck, build, tests. Sources are TypeScript under `src/`; `lib/` is build
output and is git-ignored, because the `prepare`/`prepack` hooks rebuild it
wherever the package is consumed and the published tarball carries the built
copy through the `files` allowlist.

A profile can install this bundle as a `link:` to a working copy, in which case
that copy's `lib/` is what the Host imports: rebuild after changing `src/`, or
the Host keeps running the previous build.

`node --test test/*.test.mjs` covers the pieces that fail silently in
production: the NDJSON → `StreamChunk` translation for both backends
(`src/frames.ts` framing, `src/parse.ts` Anthropic events, `src/responses.ts`
Responses events), the RSA sign-in handshake (`src/signin.ts`), the request
projections (`src/anthropic.ts`, `src/responses.ts`), and the card's slot
registration, credential and model-selection wiring (`src/client.ts`, loaded
under a stubbed module loader in `test/client.test.mjs`). The tests import the
built `lib/`, because that is what the Harness actually runs. Only
`src/index.ts` touches the Harness runtime.

Two install-time facts worth knowing: the Host half is re-imported only by a
profile restart (ESM caches by URL), and the client half is composed from the
Loader's entries at Host boot, so adding or removing `exports["./client"]` takes
a restart too — after that it is served per request under a content hash, so
client-side edits reach the browser on the next load.

plugins.description: 官方 DSH 内核补丁的数据化版本：10 条自包含补丁 + 自适应应用器（自己找安装位置、逐个备份、语法检查、一键回退），五种打法、零硬编码路径。仅支持 DSH 1.5，后续会跟进更新。 / Official DSH core patches as data: ten patches plus an adaptive applier. Five ways to apply. DSH 1.5 only.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-patch-library

**The official DSH core patches, as data — and five ways to apply them.**

**官方 DSH 内核补丁的数据化版本 —— 10 条补丁，5 种打法。**

Ten self-contained patches for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` and `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, plus a small
applier that finds *your* DSH installation by itself. No hard-coded paths, no personal information
anywhere in this repository, no network access required.

十条自成体系的补丁，覆盖 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 与 `@earendil-works/pi-ai`；配一个小巧的应用器，
它会**自己找到你的 DSH 安装位置**。零硬编码路径、仓库里没有任何个人信息、全程不需要联网。

> 🌐 **中文完整说明（推荐中文读者从这里开始）** → **[README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md)**
>
> 中文读者还应该看这两份：[`教程-安装与官方补丁` 里的补丁库章节](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-context-reclaim/blob/main/tutorial-install-and-official-patches.zh-CN.md)
> 与 [给 agent 的中文提示词](PROMPT.zh-CN.md)。

> Built for `@deepseek-ai/dsh` **0.1.5-rc.2** (the 1.5 line). Every patch records the exact
> sha256 of both the file it expects and the file it produces, so the applier can tell you
> `exact` / `applied` / `conflict` before it touches anything.

---

## Why this repository exists

Some fixes cannot be shipped as a plugin: they have to run *inside* an official file, in the middle
of a function that Cordis does not expose as a seam. Four of those fixes were already published as
plugins (`dsh-context-reclaim`, `dsh-capability-composer`, `dsh-composer-launcher`,
`dsh-aux-degrade`). The rest — plus the ones that only matter if you want the full set — live here,
as ordinary unified diffs that anyone can read, review, apply, revert, or regenerate.

Nothing here is a binary blob and nothing here is magic: `patches/<id>/change.diff` is a normal
patch, and `manifest.json` is the metadata that lets a script apply it safely and reversibly.

## The ten patches

| id | package → file | kind | size | restart | already handled by a plugin? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dsh-llm-writable-request` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` → `lib/index.js` | lines | +18 −1 | yes | **yes — `dsh-context-reclaim`** |
| `agent-loop-snapshot-prompt` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop` → `lib/index.js` | lines | +97 −20 | yes | no |
| `llm-pi-ai-system-prompt` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` → `lib/index.js` | lines | +96 −54 | yes | no |
| `compaction-pruner` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner` → `lib/index.js` | lines | +354 −14 | yes | no |
| `ui-renderer-turntail` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer` → `lib/client.js` | lines | +9 −1 | no | no |
| `ui-sidebar-wrap` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar` → `lib/lib-client.js` | **regex** | +1 −1 | no | no |
| `session-format-v1-to-v2` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v1-to-v2` → `lib/index.js` | lines | +2 −1 | yes | no |
| `session-persistence-jsonl` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` → `lib/worker.cjs` | lines | +2 −1 | yes | no |
| `mcp-client` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` → `lib/index.js` | lines | +59 −6 | yes | no |
| `pi-ai-max-tokens-floor` | `@earendil-works/pi-ai` → `dist/api/simple-options.js` | lines | +11 −1 | yes | no |

Every patch has its own `patches/<id>/NOTES.md` with **what it changes, when you want it, how to
verify it, and what to do if it does not fit your build** — in English and Chinese.

`ui-sidebar-wrap` is a **regex** patch on purpose: the sidebar's class prefix is a build hash, so a
line diff would be invalidated by any rebuild. `patches/<id>/change.json` stores the pattern and its
explicit inverse.

## Five ways to apply them

Pick whichever matches how you like to work. All five are documented step by step in
[`docs/methods.md`](docs/methods.md) (Chinese: [`docs/methods.zh-CN.md`](docs/methods.zh-CN.md)).

| | method | command |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | script (recommended) | `node apply.mjs --check` then `node apply.mjs --apply --all` |
| **B** | `git apply` | `cd <pkg dir> && git apply -p1 <library>/patches/<id>/change.diff` |
| **C** | your own AI agent | paste the block from [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) and let it do A or B for you |
| **D** | regenerate for your build | `node tools/make-patch.mjs --file <patched> --orig <pristine> --pkg <pkg> --rel <rel>` |
| **E** | revert | `node apply.mjs --revert --all`, or restore any `*.orig` by hand |

All ten diffs were verified with `git apply -p1 --check` inside the package directory, so method B
works on every one of them.

### Method A in full

```bash
node apply.mjs --list                 # what is in here
node apply.mjs --roots                # which DSH installations were found on this machine
node apply.mjs --check                # per-file state: exact / applied / conflict / missing
node apply.mjs --apply --all          # apply everything that fits
node apply.mjs --apply --only mcp-client,compaction-pruner
node apply.mjs --revert --all         # put every .orig backup back
```

`--check` reports one of:

| state | meaning |
|---|---|
| `exact` | the file is the pristine version this library was built from — applying is safe |
| `applied` | the file already equals the patched version, nothing to do |
| `variant` | same version, different build (hash differs) but the hunks still fit — needs `--allow-variant`, or method D |
| `conflict` | the hunks do not fit. **Nothing is written.** Use method D to regenerate for your build |
| `missing` | that package is not part of the installation that was found |

### What the applier guarantees

* **It finds your installation, it does not assume one.** `--root`, `$DSH_APP_ROOT`,
  `$DSH_INSTALL_ROOT`, `$DSH_HOME` (including `profiles/*`), the running process's own DSH path,
  a `node` resolution from the current directory, and a bounded scan of the usual install locations
  for Windows / macOS / Linux — see `lib/discover.mjs`. `--root` means *exactly* that root, never
  that root plus whatever else was found.
* **`.orig` is sacred.** A backup is written once, next to the file, and never overwritten. If a
  `.orig` already exists, it is reused.
* **Every edit is syntax-checked.** `node --check` runs after each write; on failure the backup is
  restored immediately and the patch is reported as failed.
* **A hunk that does not fit is a conflict, never a guess.** The engine matches a hunk's old side
  exactly, exactly once, near the position it was recorded at.
* **It only writes inside the resolved root.** Nothing under `$DSH_HOME` is touched except, if you
  explicitly point `--root` at a profile directory, that profile's own `node_modules` copy of a
  package.

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` a requested action failed or conflicted, `2` no installation found.

## If you already run the four DSH plugins

You can skip `dsh-llm-writable-request` — `dsh-context-reclaim` takes over that path from inside the
plugin, with the official patch reverted. `--check` says so explicitly:

```
= dsh-llm-writable-request     already    node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm/lib/index.js
    not needed: the dsh-context-reclaim plugin already handles this
```

The other nine are independent of the plugins: install neither, one, or both.

## Self-test

```bash
node verify.mjs
```

Offline, no DSH installation required. It checks that every diff parses and its hunk counts agree,
that the declared marker really is added by its patch, that the apply/revert engine round-trips on
synthetic samples, that a duplicated context is rejected instead of guessed, that the regex patch
round-trips through any class prefix — and that **no file in this repository contains a drive
letter, a personal home directory or a private workspace name** (that scan is part of the test
suite, not a promise).

`verify.mjs` finishes with a read-only `--check` summary of whatever installation it finds.

## Repository layout

```
apply.mjs             the applier: --list --roots --check --apply --revert --show
verify.mjs            offline self-test + personal-information scan
manifest.json         every patch's metadata: hashes, sizes, markers, risk, why, applyWhen
lib/manifest.mjs      manifest loading and schema checks
lib/discover.mjs      finds DSH installations (fully adaptive, platform-aware)
lib/unified.mjs       unified-diff parse / apply / revert engine
lib/backup.mjs        .orig backup and restore
lib/hash.mjs          sha256 helpers
patches/<id>/change.diff   the patch itself

[English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh.md)

# dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth

**Use the AI subscriptions you already pay for as LLM providers in DeepSeek Harness — no API key.**

Sign in once per provider from **Settings → Subscriptions** and that provider's models join the session model picker, with its plan quota shown live next to the connection. Tokens stay on your machine; every request streams through the provider's own API.

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth)
[![Licence: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

## Supported providers

| Provider | What you get | Sign-in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Kimi Code** | `kimi-for-coding`, `k3` (1M), `k3-256k` — read from the endpoint's own model list | OAuth device flow (show code, confirm in browser) |
| **Grok (X Premium)** | whatever the account's own model list reports (e.g. `grok-4.7`), **⚡ lightspeed** fast variant | Browser OAuth (auto-redirect) |
| **Google Antigravity** | Claude Sonnet/Opus, Gemini Flash, GPT-OSS, with reasoning tiers — read from the account's own list | Google account OAuth |
| **GLM (BigModel)** | whatever the coding host lists (e.g. `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.3-flash`) | ZCode browser sign-in (polled) |
| **Volcengine Ark** | the plan's own coding models | Volcengine SSO |
| **Xiaomi MiMo** | MiMo's own model list, with the app's two-model set as the fallback | Xiaomi account (QR / password) |
| **WorkBuddy (国内版)** | Hy, GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, MiniMax models | Browser OAuth (Tencent) |

Every provider also feeds the **`auto`** route, which spans them all: pick `auto` and the harness walks your enabled models in order until one answers.

## Features

- **One sign-in per provider** — no API keys to find, paste, or rotate. The plugin runs the provider's own OAuth/device flow and keeps the token on disk (`~/.dsh/plugins/kimi-oauth/auth.json`, mode `0600`).
- **Live plan usage** — the Settings card and the composer chip show each account's remaining quota (Kimi's 5-hour / weekly windows + credit, Grok's weekly credit, Antigravity's Gemini + Claude buckets, GLM/Ark/MiMo/WorkBuddy credits), with a meter and reset time.
- **Model picker integration** — each provider's models appear in the session picker with context windows and reasoning tiers; hide or re-order them per provider.
- **Catalogs come from the provider, not from this build** — every route reads its own model list once and caches it as the provider's table, so a model released, renamed or retired server-side shows up (or disappears) without a plugin update. Signing in and the Settings **refresh models** action are what re-read it; browsing the picker never spends a request.
- **⚡ Fast / lightspeed variants** — for models that have one (e.g. Grok 4.7 → `grok-4.7-build-fast`), a bolt button beside the model selector switches to the fast variant; it reads as a reasoning rung so the base model always stays selectable.
- **Cross-account pool** — sign in to several accounts on one provider; the plugin draws on the next account when one's allowance runs out.
- **Auto fallback** — `auto` moves to the next enabled model when a provider refuses the preferred one (renamed, rate-limited, out of quota), and stops falling back once a stream has started.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth
```

Then restart DeepSeek Harness and open **Settings → Subscriptions** (订阅).

To install a specific version, or straight from the repository:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth@0.10.2
dsh plugin --profile web add github:EricFL1998/dsh-subscription-oauth
```

## How to use

1. **Open Settings → Subscriptions.** You see one card per provider; signed-in providers sort to the front, `auto` leads.
2. **Connect** a provider. A browser window (or a device code) starts the provider's own sign-in. Finish it there — the card updates by itself.
3. **Pick a model.** The provider's models now appear in the composer model picker, and the chip shows live usage.
4. **Expand a card** to manage accounts (set default, sign out, refresh token), toggle which models appear, re-order them, add a model id this build doesn't know yet, and see the credential file / endpoints.

> **Tip:** to use a different account on a provider, sign out first, then connect again — the browser sign-in follows whichever account the provider's page is signed in with.

## What it registers

| Surface | What appears |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.llm` | the `kimi`, `grok`, `antigravity`, `glm`, `ark`, `mimo`, `workbuddy` and `auto` provider routes (models, reasoning, streaming) |
| Settings | a **Subscriptions** section: one card per provider |
| Model picker | each provider's own models, plus **`auto`** spanning them all |
| Composer chip | live plan usage for the provider in force |

## Hiding a provider

To keep a provider's models out of the picker without uninstalling, drop it from the route list in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yml
# $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml
plugins:
  dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth:
    providers: [kimi, grok, antigravity, glm, ark, mimo, workbuddy]
```

Omit the ones you don't want. The list defaults to every implemented route.

## Security

- Credentials are stored locally at `~/.dsh/plugins/kimi-oauth/auth.json` (mode `0600`, written atomically), one section per provider.
- The plugin talks only to the providers' own hosts and OAuth endpoints — no telemetry, no third-party relay.
- Your subscriptions only; nothing is shared across machines.

## Develop

See the [developer README](README.dev.md) for the full wire protocol, token lifetimes, troubleshooting, and how to run the test suite.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.readme_text:
# Onto Space Panel for DeepSeek Harness

A compact Onto space picker and a side panel for declarations, resident agents,
memory artifacts, templates and objects. Select what belongs in the current chat;
the active context remains visible above the composer.

## Features

- Connect to Onto on first use: enter your MCP endpoint and API key, verify
  access, then select a space. Reuse an existing Harness connection automatically.
- Search and select available Onto spaces.
- Open the space panel with **Обзор**.
- Read an accepted/current space declaration and attach it to the chat.
- Inspect resident agents and their charters. Selecting a valid active resident
  loads its accepted charter and constitution into the current chat.
- Search and page through accepted memory artifacts, read their contents and
  explicitly attach or disconnect them.
- Browse templates and objects, then include selected objects in the conversation.
- Keep selections and context separate for each chat and each selected realm.
- Change context through the `select_onto_space` and
  `configure_onto_chat_context` model tools when the user requests it.

The UI is currently in Russian. Names and descriptions are supplied by Onto.
An agent selection gives the current Harness conversation a resident role;
it does not launch a separate agent process or external agent broker.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with its Web UI or Desktop application.
- Your Onto MCP endpoint URL and personal API key, or an existing authenticated
  Harness MCP connection named **`onto`**.
- Harness's writable credential provider for the first-use setup form. Standard
  local profiles use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials-local`.
- The connection must expose `list_available_realms`, `about_realm`,
  `list_realm_agents`, `get_realm_agent`, `search_memory_artifacts`,
  `get_memory_artifact`, `get_memory_artifact_by_path`, `search_templates`,
  `search_objects` and `get_entity` for their respective panel features.

Host integration was developed against DeepSeek Harness **0.2.0-rc.2**.
Other releases are not yet verified. Harness is in developer preview and its
extension interfaces can change.

## Install a release tarball

Download the package `.tgz` from the project's release and install it into a
Web-capable profile. For example:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-onto-space-panel-1.2.1.tgz
```

Release downloads: https://github.com/hope4b/dsh-onto-space-panel/releases

You can also install the tagged GitHub source, which already contains the built
browser entry point and has no install-time build script:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:hope4b/dsh-onto-space-panel#v1.2.1
```

In Desktop, use **Plugins** to install the downloaded bundle where supported by
your version. The tarball already contains the browser bundle; no install-time
build script or extra build permission is needed.

If this plugin was previously loaded manually by an absolute-path row in
`cordis.patch.yml`, disable that old row before enabling the packaged bundle.
Do not run two copies: they register the same tools and API routes.

Restart Harness after installing or replacing the bundle. Select an Onto space
above the composer and press **Обзор** to open its panel. Use **В контекст** to
attach a declaration or memory artifact. A role or material can be removed using
the `×` next to its context label.

## Connect Onto MCP

### First-use setup (recommended)

1. Install the plugin and restart Harness.
2. Click **Onto → Подключить** above the composer.
3. Enter your MCP endpoint URL and personal API key, then press **Подключить**.
   The key field expects only the value. A pasted `X-Onto-Api-Key: value` line
   is accepted too: the plugin removes the header name before sending or storing it.
4. The plugin checks access with `list_available_realms` before saving. After
   success, select a space from the list. An empty list means the connection
   works but no accessible spaces were returned.

Obtain the endpoint and key from your Onto administrator. The form uses HTTPS
and the `X-Onto-Api-Key` header; localhost HTTP is supported for development.
It requires a direct MCP endpoint, without credentials or query parameters in
the URL. Authentication redirects are rejected.

The connection belongs to the active Harness profile. Keys are stored through
Harness's credential provider, not in plugin configuration, browser storage or
chat messages. With the standard local provider, the managed credential file is
`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`. This is local credential storage, not a claim of
OS keychain encryption. The server address and credential reference are stored
under `$DSH_HOME/storages/onto-connections/`, keyed by the profile location.
The plugin restores its own MCP connection on startup without editing profile YAML.

Open **Подключение** in the space picker, or **Подключение Onto** in the side
panel, to update a connection created by the plugin. A blank key reuses the saved
key only when the endpoint stays the same. Changing the endpoint or account key
requires choosing spaces and attaching context again; old chat context is not
automatically applied to the new connection.

If Harness already provides a server named `onto`, the plugin reuses it and
skips onboarding. Those external settings remain managed in Harness; the panel
does not overwrite or migrate that connection. A configured but unavailable
connection is shown as configured, with errors when loading spaces.

### Manual Harness configuration (fallback)

Use this when your deployment manages MCP centrally or does not provide a writable
credential provider. If the profile already has an Onto connection, do not add
a second one.

1. Obtain your Onto **MCP endpoint URL** and personal API key from your Onto
   administrator. Use the MCP endpoint, not the ordinary Onto website URL.
2. Open the active profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: normally
   `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` for Web or
   `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\cordis.patch.yml` for Windows Desktop.
   A custom `DSH_HOME` changes the `.dsh` location.
3. Append the following patch, replacing the placeholder URL. If an Onto entry
   already exists, update it instead of creating a duplicate. The server name
   must be exactly `onto`.

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: mcp-onto
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: onto
        transport: streamable-http
        url: https://YOUR-ONTO-MCP-HOST/mcp
        headers:
          X-Onto-Api-Key: !!js process.env.ONTO_API_KEY
```

This example uses Onto's `X-Onto-Api-Key` header. Confirm the authentication
scheme with your server administrator if your deployment differs.
A copy is available in [examples/onto-mcp.patch.yml](examples/onto-mcp.patch.yml).

4. Set `ONTO_API_KEY` in the environment of the process that starts Harness.
   For Web on Windows, start it from the same PowerShell window:

```powershell
$env:ONTO_API_KEY = 'YOUR_PERSONAL_API_KEY'
dsh --profile web
```

For Windows Desktop, fully quit Harness first, set the variable above, then
launch the executable from that same PowerShell window. For the default installer
location:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\DeepSeek Harness.exe"
```

Launching via an existing desktop shortcut does not inherit a variable set only
in this PowerShell window. The variable must be available on every launch.
Enter your real key locally; do not commit it or share terminal history containing it.

5. Open the space selector above the composer. Your accessible spaces should
   appear. You can also ask the model to call `mcp__onto__list_available_realms`.

If connection fails, check the endpoint and network access first. A `401` or
`403` response usually indicates authentication or access rights. If the tools
work in chat but the panel cannot find them, check that `serverName` is `onto`.
Missing agent or memory tools affect those sections separately; an empty list
can also mean your account has no access to those resources.

The transport and environment-variable syntax follow the official
[Harness MCP client configuration](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepse

# dsh-plugin-backup

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A backup plugin for DeepSeek Harness: it packages `$DSH_HOME` into verifiable,
restorable, downloadable archives by category, and can mirror those backups to
GitHub. Everything is available from three faces that share one engine and one
single-run lock: the **Web settings page**, the **model tool surface**, and a
**CLI session**.

- Naming: `dsh-backup-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHmmss>`
- Categories: `settings`, `skills`, `plugins`, `sessions`, `storages`
- Per backup: **download / verify / restore / delete**
- Settings: **backup path**, **backup interval**, per-category switches, retention count,
  verify-after-create, per-category archive ceiling, GitHub sync
- No build step and no third-party runtime dependency: the host half is plain ESM,
  the browser half is a hand-writable CommonJS factory the shell loads as-is

## Install

```powershell
# local checkout (development)
dsh plugin --profile web add file:C:/path/to/dsh-plugin-backup

# or from GitHub
dsh plugin --profile web add github:shiinakaze/dsh-plugin-backup
```

The Desktop app manages its own `desktop` profile: install through its plugin
manager (or `dsh plugin --profile desktop add …`) and restart the app.

`dsh plugin add` both records the dependency and appends the package name to
`dsh.profile.bundles` (one composition layer). Reload or restart the Web
interface afterwards, then open **Settings → Data backup**.

> **Runtime support.** The plugin targets the `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.7 and 0.2.0
> lines: `peerDependencies` declare `^0.1.7-rc.2 || ^0.2.0-rc.1` for `dsh-tools`
> and `dsh-typert-protocol`, and `engines.dsh` mirrors that window. This matters
> on 0.2.0, whose boot performs a compatibility preflight against the running
> runtime and **refuses to install or mount a bundle whose dsh peers it cannot
> satisfy** — an exact pin to one rc would be rejected. The two branches are not
> cosmetic: package managers resolve with npm's prerelease rule, under which a
> prerelease is admitted only when some comparator pins its exact version tuple,
> so one `>=0.1.7-rc.2 <0.3.0` window silently drops `0.2.0-rc.1` and
> `0.2.0-rc.2` and fails `npm install` with `ERESOLVE`. Keep the window in
> `package.json` in step with the APIs the plugin actually uses.

> A `file:` install is a **snapshot**: the profile keeps its own copy, so after
> changing this package's source you must `dsh plugin --profile web remove <name>`
> and add it again. The measured verification log lives in
> [docs/verify.md](docs/verify.md).

> This is a DSH plugin, not a plain dependency: the host half injects the `tools`
> service declared in its schema, and the browser half is discovered through the
> `dsh.client` declaration in `package.json`. Without `$DSH_HOME` the plugin falls
> back to `~/.dsh`; in a non-Web profile (no `webServer` service) only *download*
> is unavailable — every other feature and tool still works.

## The page

Settings → **Data backup**:

| Block | Contents |
|---|---|
| Backup settings | Backup path (empty = `C:\Users\<user>\dsh_backups` on Windows, `~/dsh_backups` elsewhere; `~` and `${DSH_HOME}` are expanded), interval (off / 15 min / hourly / 6 h / daily / weekly), backups to keep, verify right after creating |
| Backup categories | The **selection** for a run: check the categories to include, with select-all / select-none; the button names the current choice ("Back up now (3 categories)") and is disabled with a hint while nothing is selected |
| Existing backups | Per row: id, creation time, file count, size, category tags, last verdict; actions are a **download** menu (one category or the manifest), **verify**, **preview restore**, **restore**, and **delete** (restore and delete take a second click to confirm; delete is the destructive-colored one) |
| GitHub sync | Enable switch, `owner/repo`, branch, subdirectory, token environment variable, whether a token was detected, and **push / pull** |

"Back up now" covers only the checked categories; saving the settings also makes that
selection the default for scheduled runs.

Settings are written to the plugin's own user layer at
`$DSH_HOME/dsh-plugin-backup/settings.json` (`0600`); the deployment baseline stays
in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and the two are shallow-merged (user wins).

## Layout on disk

```
<backupPath>/
  dsh-backup-20260930-141205/
    manifest.json           # schema version, host facts, per-category files/bytes/sha256/archive, last verdict
    settings.tar.gz         # one gzipped USTAR archive per category
    skills.tar.gz
    plugins.tar.gz
```

The manifest is written last and atomically, so "a directory with a manifest" is a
complete backup. Intermediate files carry a `.part` suffix while a run is in
flight; residue from a crash is cleaned up or ignored at the start of the next run.

## Categories and exclusions

| key | Sources (relative to `$DSH_HOME`) | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `settings` | `settings.yaml*`, `cordis.patch.yml*`, `.credentials.yaml*`, `.anonymous-user-id`, `dsh-skill-hub.json`, `skills-market-sync.json` | on |
| `skills` | `skills-management/**` | on |
| `plugins` | `profiles/*/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `cordis.patch.yml*`, plus `plugins/**` | on |
| `sessions` | `sessions/**` | off |
| `storages` | `storages/**` | off |

Always excluded: `node_modules` and `.git*` at any depth, symbolic links, and the
backup root itself — so keeping the store inside `$DSH_HOME` never recurses.

### Measured on a real harness home (`settings` + `plugins` + `skills`)

| Category | Files | Raw | Archive | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `settings` | 5 | 2.0 KB | 1.3 KB | < 0.1 s |
| `plugins` | 39 | 1.24 MB | 1.12 MB | 0.2 s |
| `skills` | 29 356 | 342.5 MB | 144.8 MB | ≈ 50 s |

Creation and verification are streaming (flat memory; measured RSS went 57 MB →
158 MB), so a category is never held in memory. That is why the default ceiling is
**512 MiB**: a realistic skills tree already passes 100 MiB compressed. Raise
`maxArchiveBytes` in the settings if yours is larger, or leave `skills` out and
back it up by hand. With retention 20 and `skills` enabled the store can reach ~3 GB.

## GitHub sync

1. Enable sync on the settings page and fill in `owner/repo` (a full URL also works),
   the branch, and the subdirectory.
2. Token resolution, in order:
   - an environment variable — `DSH_BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN` by default (renameable in settings);
   - the state file `$DSH_HOME/dsh-plugin-backup/github-token.json` holding `{"token": "…"}`, mode `0600`.
   The token is read from nowhere else and never written to config, logs, or tool output.
3. **Push** uploads file by file through the Contents API, archives first and
   `manifest.json` last; a backup the remote already holds with the same content is
   skipped. **Pull** downloads only the backups missing locally and verifies every
   archive against the sha256 in its manifest — a mismatch discards that backup and
   reports why.

Remote layout: `<subdir>/<backupId>/{manifest.json,<category>.tar.gz}`.

## Model tools

| Tool | Parameters | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `backup_run` | `categories?`, `label?` | Create a backup now |
| `backup_list` | `limit?` | List backups, newest first |
| `backup_verify` | `id` | Recompute sha256 and re-read the tar structure, per category |
| `backup_restore` | `id`, `categories?`, `dryRun?`, `force?` | Restore; `dryRun` only reports the plan |
| `backup_delete` | `id`, `force?` | Delete; the newest backup is protected while an older one exists |
| `backup_sync` | `direction`, `ids?` | Push to or pull from GitHub |

A typical loop: `backup_run` before a risky change, then `backup_verify` and
`backup_restore` afterwards. `backup_restore` verifies first and refuses a corrupt
backup unless `force` is set.

## Safety boundaries

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Path traversal | Backup ids must match `^dsh-backup-\d{8}-\d{6}$`; archive entries refuse absolute paths, drive letters, and `..` |
| Corruption | `verify` names the category and the expected/actual sha256; `restore` refuses by default and, under `force`, skips that category and reports it |
| Irrevers

# shisan-xinuo-dsh-plugin

**DeepSeek Harness（DSH）运行时治理插件**——把工程纪律从提示词层下沉到执行层：模型尝试跳过前置条件、调用不该调的工具、或凭自述宣告完成时，由宿主扩展面上的确定性检查介入，而不是依赖模型回忆规则。源码单文件引擎（`src/shisan-xinuo-core.ts`）+ 数据层规则包（`content/`），一切行为面可用真实运行证据复查。

> **状态：工程验收版（内部）· 未发行。** 有效性对照已完成机制验证轮（四臂×3 任务×3 轮，36 会话，A/B/C/D 含干净 DSH 基线）：运行时控制组的收口合规 5/9 vs 纪律文本组 0/9；行为有效性待 n≥5 补样本轮判定。

## 能力矩阵（主张=状态标签制，证据可复查）

| # | 主张 | 状态 | 宿主面 vs 插件增量 | 证据 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | L3 危险操作在工具执行管线内被程序性拦截（命中→审批询问，宿主侧不可绕过该检查） | **已实现有测试**（正则覆盖 6 域+9 豁免+嵌套 shell 形态） | 审批卡 UI 与 pre-execute 管线为宿主原生；插件供红线规则、误拦豁免、形态封堵 | 单测 8正10负+23例+58误拦样本；真实宿主 16 次拦截+审批链 3 次全通 |
| 2 | 收口验证依据真实退出码而非模型自述（discipline_gate 工具：宿主真跑 cmd，声明与实测不符=打回） | **已实现有测试**（四臂实验中 3 次打回无效验证——模型每次修正后重过） | 命令执行/退出码采集走宿主；判定语义（三态+拒跑）为插件自有 | tests/gate-tool 44 例；E1 报告 |

| 4 | 工具预算器：按任务判级裁剪工具面（restrict 掩码），测量以每请求线缆真值为准 | **已实现有测试**（25→8 工具，-58.6%；同 agent 会话中途收窄实证） | restrict/request 事件为宿主扩展面；策略与 always-allow 为插件自有 | tests/budget 21 例 |
| 5 | 行为遥测与对账：exec-log 全落账，tally `--report/--check` 出数+对账（白名单/不变量/快照，抓植入差错） | **已实现有测试** | 插件自有（日志为插件所写，非宿主审计面） | tests/tally 16 例（5 类攻击样本全被抓） |

| 7 | 拦截覆盖完备性 | **已知边界**——枚举型正则有天花板；「目标替代」（用 write 清空代替删除+对偷换目标做真验证）不可在正则层修，指向 v2 任务状态机 | — | docs/e1-v1-report §3、e1-v4 §三 |
| 8 | 任务控制器（状态机+验收条件持有）/ 受控执行器 | **规划（v2，待批）**——收口强制缺口（工具存在≠模型必用，删除任务自发调用率 1/3）由本版闭合 | — | docs/product-recalibration-20261013.md |

**诚实条款**：本插件保证「过程可审计、收口有真值」，不保证「模型更聪明」；三命题分立——机制存在（✓）≠机制有效（待补样本轮）≠产品有效（待对照终判）。审批卡、命令执行、事件管线均为 DSH 原生能力，插件的净增量在**可替换的策略、真值判定语义与强制闭环**。

## 代价与风险（如实）

- **收口验证是一条新的执行通道**：`discipline_gate`（及 `cmd_exit0` 断言、宿主收口复核）会在插件侧直接执行你声明的验证命令——护栏=危险域清单＋被拒命令指纹（10 分钟），**不是安全沙箱**；清单覆盖面之外（目标替代、重定向覆写、脚本清空等）不拦，与 pwsh 通道同一天花板；仅存在于上游 `.dsh/rules.yaml` 的自定义规则也不覆盖此通道。2026-10-13 加固：`discipline_task` 的 replace 仅作用于工具自登记断言——**用户原文推导断言恒保留，模型不可移除/改写**；并支持**判据锚点（pinned）**：`SHISANUO_ASSERTIONS` 可在会话外钉死断言（模型侧不可见），形成三级判据「pinned > auto（默认关）> tool」——**2026-10-13 起启发式推导默认退位**（SHISANUO_ASSERT_LAYER=1 可重新启用）。
- **一致性≠有效性**：`claimedExit` 比对只抓「谎报退出码」；`echo ok; exit 0` 类与目标无关的命令会通过（命令与目标的相关性无机器校验；资源断言仅覆盖可枚举路径）。
- **收口强制会注入一条以用户信封发送的指令**：turn-stopping 触发时经 `steer` 注入（信封 `source=user` 为宿主接口约束），文本以固定前缀 `[十三希诺收口强制]` 显式标注来源；插件按该前缀排除自身注入，避免自我循环。**在界面上它呈现为一条"用户发言"**——请勿把它当作你自己说过的话：宿主投递 API（`send`／`followup`／`steer`／`inject`）的参数类型均为 `UserMessage`，故"显示为用户"是接口约束而非本插件选择；唯一不具用户外观的通道是 `inject()`，但它**不唤醒**驱动，承担不了"强制回合不结束"的语义，因此强制类必须走 `steer`，非强制的上下文提示（如工具目录、预算态）应改用 `inject()`。
- **「可用但禁用」的能力面（如实披露）**：宿主另外开放了两条更强通道，本插件**主动不用**——① `ctx.sessions.registerMessageProjection()` 可在**消息被接受前改写内容**；② `agent.ctx` 上可注册**同名的 per-agent 工具变体**（改写宿主工具在该会话内的语义）。理由：前者改的是**会话记录本身**，而会话日志是本项目的证据底座；后者若用于放宽/美化判定，等于把治理机制变成新的攻击面。**本插件的红线：这两条只允许用于"加强"方向（加审计／加证据／加来源标注），不得用于放宽或改写证据。**
- **遥测日志默认明文落盘**：`<repo>/logs/exec-log.jsonl`（命令截断 200 字符、stdout/stderr 尾 300 字符；写入前对常见密钥形态自动脱敏——非穷尽）。可用 `SHISANUO_LOG_DIR` 指到私密目录；`SHISANUO_LOG_DISABLE=1` 可整体关闭落盘（不留痕环境；启动以 stdout 一行声明，代价=放弃审计底座）；日志不入库（.gitignore）。
- **循环防护弱于社区同类**：收口强制=每回合最多 1 次 steer；无 `impossible` 类 hook 逃生口——被阻塞时以「如实报告」收口（宿主记 `unverified`/`assertion-unresolved`）。
- **开发态绑定**：无 `dsh.bundle` manifest（仅 `file://` patch 挂载）、绑定 cordis `4.0.5-alpha.1`、未发行——宿主 alpha API 变更可能破坏兼容。
- 一句话：**不要把本插件当作安全边界**——拦截面=枚举覆盖，验证面=真退出码；两者治「过程」，不承诺「安全」。

# dsh-opencode-go-catalog

A live-maintained OpenCode Go model catalog for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
(DSH). Membership is rebuilt from the live roster plus the docs endpoint table on every sync — new
models appear, retired ones drop out, no hand work. A curated snapshot stays as the offline fallback.

**Status:** 0.2.0 · auto membership · 33 models live (2026-10-13), incl. **Cat Jam Free** (`cat-jam-free`)

- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Installation](#installation)

- [Commands & scripts](#commands--scripts)
- [Fresh reasoning efforts](#fresh-reasoning-efforts)
